classification.difficultyReason: Factor each perfect-square quadratic, locate its double zero and reflect the y-intercept to obtain a third point for the sketch.

content.prompt: Sketch these parabolas involving perfect squares. Hint: Begin by factoring the quadratic. In each case, symmetry will be needed to find a third point on the parabola.

answer.short: $y=(x-3)^2$: concave up; vertex $(3,0)$; axis $x=3$; passes through $(0,9)$ and $(6,9)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-6x+9\\y&=(x-3)^2\end{align*}$$
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the parabola is concave up. Setting $y=0$ gives
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)^2&=0\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Thus the vertex is $(3,0)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=3$. At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-3)^2\\y&=9\end{align*}$$
Reflecting $(0,9)$ in $x=3$ gives $(6,9)$. Sketch a smooth parabola through these three points, touching the $x$-axis at $(3,0)$.

spec.description: Complete solution graph with double zero at 3, y-intercept 9, reflected point (6,9), and dashed symmetry and horizontal guides. No grid is supplied in the source.
spec.mathematics: y=(x-3)^2; vertex (3,0); symmetry axis x=3; points (0,9) and (6,9).

answer.short: $y=-(x-1)^2$: concave down; vertex $(1,0)$; axis $x=1$; passes through $(0,-1)$ and $(2,-1)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-x^2+2x-1\\y&=-(x^2-2x+1)\\y&=-(x-1)^2\end{align*}$$
The coefficient of $x^2$ is negative, so the parabola is concave down. Setting $y=0$ gives
$$\begin{align*}-(x-1)^2&=0\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Thus the vertex is $(1,0)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=1$. At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0-1)^2\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
Reflecting $(0,-1)$ in $x=1$ gives $(2,-1)$. Sketch a smooth parabola through these three points, touching the $x$-axis at $(1,0)$.
